candidates.authors: Ke Guo, Zheng Huang, Wei Wang, Wei-Li Song, Shuqiang Jiao
candidates.abstract: Aluminium-graphite batteries offer low cost and intrinsic high safety. However, the voltage window mostly remains limited because conventional chloroaluminate ionic-liquid electrolytes with Lewis-acidic Al2Cl7−([AlCl3–AlCl4]−) anions are intrinsically moisture-sensitive and unstable beyond 2.5 V. To extend the voltage window, a polytetrafluoroethylene/AlF3 framework‑confined, fluorine-rich chloroaluminate ionic-liquid composite quasi-solid-state electrolyte cosolvated with 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl ether is designed for constructing stable aluminium-graphite batteries with a cut-off voltage of 3.0 V. With the presence of AlF3, the Al2Cl7− is regulated through AlF3-associated chloroaluminate interactions, which reduces its activity and suppresses its electrochemical decomposition in the range of 2.5–3.0 V. Meanwhile, the fluorinated ether coordinates with the AlCl3 units in Al2Cl7− and promotes the formation of a fluorine-rich artificial interface on the graphite, essentially improving the electrochemical stability via alleviating electrochemical decomposition of AlCl4− up to 3.0 V. Furthermore, ion transport channels could be well maintained during large mechanical deformation induced by anion-intercalation/deintercalation of graphite interlayer. Therefore, the Al|electrolyte|graphite cells deliver discharge capacity beyond 137 mAh g−1 up to 3.0 V (specific current: 5.0 A g−1) (compared to 64 mAh g−1, charged up to 2.5 V at 5.0 A g−1) along with stable cycles beyond 35,000, demonstrating long-term high-voltage operation in rechargeable aluminium–graphite batteries. Aluminium–graphite batteries are limited by electrolyte decomposition above 2.5 V. Here, authors regulate chloroaluminate anions with a fluorine-rich, framework-confined quasi-solid-state electrolyte, enabling stable 3.0 V operation for Al | |Graphite cells.

candidates.title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin films
candidates.authors: Boxuan Zhou, Haoyang Li, Bangyao Hu, Jingxuan Zhou, Chen Li, Jingyuan Zhou, Yu Huang, Xiangfeng Duan
candidates.abstract: Abstract Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are promising laser-gain media for their direct bandgap and strong excitonic effects. However, existing TMD lasers typically rely on mechanically exfoliated or high-temperature chemical-vapor-deposition-grown materials, with their atomic-scale thickness inherently limiting the available optical gain volume. Here, we report room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS 2 (BM-MoS 2 ) thin films in whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) cavities. Using solution exfoliation and spray coating under ambient conditions, we produce area- and thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films composed of electronically decoupled MoS 2 monolayers separated by organic spacers. This layered architecture preserves the intrinsic monolayer excitonic properties while providing a tunable gain volume beyond that of an isolated monolayer. Integrated with WGM cavities, the thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films enable a balance between the quality ( Q ) and optical confinement ( $$\varGamma$$ Γ ) factors. Power-dependent measurements reveal key lasing signatures, including a threshold-like input-output crossover accompanied by linewidth narrowing at a pump power of approximately 1.4 nW, and pump-induced polarization selection. Solution-processable BM-MoS 2 thus offers a scalable gain medium for thin-film laser photonics.

candidates.title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
candidates.authors: Qiran Wu, Jingyuan Cui, Ang-Kun Wu, Yuze Meng, Dongxue Chen, Yueshan Wang, Li Yan, Lei Ma, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Shi-Zeng Lin, Su-Fei Shi, Yong-Tao Cui
candidates.abstract: Abstract Kondo insulators are paradigmatic strongly correlated materials, traditionally found in f-electron compounds. They originate from the hybridization between itinerant conduction electrons and localized magnetic moments, which opens a gap in the electronic spectrum. Two-dimensional moiré systems provide a new route to flat bands with strong electron correlation, which host localized moments at half filling. Here we report signatures, based on local conductivity measurements using microwave impedance microscopy, of a Kondo insulator in a moiré superlattice of monolayer WS 2 / bilayer WSe 2 , in which one WSe 2 layer carries flat moiré bands and the other dispersive ones. When both layers are partially doped with two holes per moiré unit cell in total, an insulating state appears when the moiré band contains less than one hole. The insulator becomes metallic above a certain threshold magnetic field, evidence for the singlet nature of the Kondo insulator, and the observed behavior is reproduced by a periodic Anderson model. Our results open a route to simulating Kondo physics in tunable moiré systems.

candidates.title: The posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell circuit mediates an anti-pruritic response
candidates.authors: Jie-Yan Zheng, Zi-Hao Wang, Jia-Yang Lin, Chao Huang, Guang-Yan Pan, Dong-Liang Xu, Xiao-Yang Hu, Shuang-Qi Gao
candidates.abstract: Notable differences between histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch have been extensively researched at peripheral and spinal levels. However, the way in which the brain processes histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch remains unknown. We discovered that the posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (pPVT)→the nucleus accumbens medial shell (NAcMed) circuit exhibits reverse response patterns to histamine-dependent or histamine-independent itch and serves as a central anti-pruritic role. Mechanistically, histamine-dependent itch activates excitatory inputs from the lateral hypothalamus (LH) to mobilise the anti-pruritic centre, thereby buffering its intensity. In cases of chronic itch, however, there is a decrease in the efficiency of the anti-pruritic circuit’s postsynaptic transmission, thereby promoting itch sensitisation. Our research reveals that histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch are processed differently in the mouse brain, offering insights into the neural mechanisms underlying chronic itch sensitization. Neural mechanisms underlying itch are not fully understood. Here authors show that the pPVT-NAcMed (posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell) circuit oppositely responds to histamine-dependent vs -independent itch, with LH inputs buffering the former, but chronic itch reduces postsynaptic efficacy, promoting sensitization and revealing differential processing.

candidates.abstract: Systematic and precise regulation of coordination environments in single-atom catalysts (SACs) remains challenging due to thermodynamic constraints and kinetic traps. Herein, we report a thermodynamic-guided strategy to tailor the local coordination of Fe single atoms on CoWO4 support by regulating oxygen chemical potential. Combining operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations, Fe1O4 is identified as the optimal configuration for hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) electrosynthesis, which delivers balanced kinetics by moderating free water dissociation for *NH3 generation and strengthening HCHO chemisorption via pronounced Fe 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization near the Fermi level. As a result, the Fe1O4 SAC achieves a HMTA yield of 0.21 mmol h−1 cm−2 with 83.04% Faradaic efficiency at 1.75 V and stability over 200 h in a flow cell. This work establishes a universal thermodynamic approach for precise coordination engineering of single-atom electrocatalysts and provides a general paradigm for kinetically balancing complex multi-intermediate electrocatalytic systems. Precise control of single-atom coordination is hindered by thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. Here, the authors report tuning Fe-O coordination on CoWO4 via oxygen chemical potential control. Optimal Fe1O4 boosts hexamethylenetetramine electrosynthesis with high yield, efficiency and stability.

candidates.title: Post-pandemic immunity debt and environmental decoupling reshape urban influenza transmission
candidates.authors: Abao Xing, Hoiman Ng, Jianlin Lin, Qianhong Ye, Henry H. Y. Tong, Yusi Li, Jianming Liang, Yi Ma, Guanmin Jiang, Kefeng Li
candidates.abstract: Relaxation of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions was followed by a global resurgence of respiratory infections, yet how accumulated population susceptibility interacts with environmental forcing and human mobility remains unclear. Here we analyse ~1.88 million clinical influenza tests from Macau (2010-2025) alongside meteorology, air quality, digital information-seeking, and independent surveillance and time-resolved viral genomes from Hong Kong, benchmarked against global surveillance data. Counterfactual inference indicates a post-pandemic excess in influenza activity consistent with immunity debt, mirroring global resurgence patterns, and an independently parameterised susceptible–exposed–infectious–recovered–susceptible model reproduces this excess (best-fit debt fraction 42%; approximate Bayesian computation posterior 58%, 95% uncertainty interval 32-77%). Susceptibility rises disproportionately in adults rather than children, whereas vaccination coverage in high-risk groups does not decline, arguing against reduced uptake as the driver. Time-varying models and convergent cross mapping reveal environmental decoupling, whereby high susceptibility weakens meteorological constraints and sustains influenza A transmission, and asymmetric suppression of influenza B. Spatiotemporal and phylogenetic evidence supports travel-linked reintroduction from ports of entry into dense neighbourhoods, and digital information-seeking shifts from lagging to leading clinical burden. These findings indicate a post-pandemic regime shift in influenza dynamics rather than a return to historical baselines, motivating adaptive, multi-source surveillance in high-density cities. Using 1.88 million clinical records from Macau and regional and global surveillance, in this study, the authors show how reduced population immunity and renewed travel reshaped post-pandemic influenza transmission and weakened its usual links with climate.

candidates.title: Epithelium stratifies via nucleation and growth induced by foam-geometric instability
candidates.authors: Shuya Fukamachi, Razib Datta, Duligengaowa Wuergezhen, Takehiko Ichikawa, Rei Yagasaki, Phoebe Leeaw, Makiko Arai, Aki Teranishi, Shuhei A. Horiguchi, Kohei Omachi, Aiko Sada, Itaru Imayoshi, Kentaro Kajiwara, Tetsuya Hiraiwa, Masanobu Oshima, Takeshi Fukuma, Hironobu Fujiwara, Satoru Okuda
candidates.abstract: Abstract Epithelial stratification, the transition from a monolayer to a multilayer structure, occurs across a wide range of phenomena. Recent studies have identified several cell behaviors as triggers, including junctional tension, cell density and geometry, and topological defects. However, how these factors drive stratification throughout the entire epithelium remains poorly understood. Here, we show that epithelial stratification proceeds through a nucleation-and-growth mechanism. Combining cell culture with three-dimensional vertex modeling, we demonstrate that multilayer origins emerge in a dispersed manner and expand across the epithelium through disordered intermediate states. candidates.title: Qubit Noise Sensing via Induced Photon Loss in a Superconducting Cavity
candidates.authors: Nitzan Kahn, Dror Garti, Uri Goldblatt, Lalit M. Joshi, Fabien Lafont, Serge Rosenblum
candidates.abstract: Characterizing noise in superconducting qubits is essential for improving coherence and gate performance. Conventional noise-sensing methods typically use the qubit itself as the sensor, which limits both accessible bandwidth and applicability during driven operation. Here, we measure qubit frequency noise by detecting the photon loss it induces in a coupled high-Q superconducting cavity. We use repeated mid-circuit qubit measurements with post-selection to separate this induced loss from intrinsic cavity decay. We validate the protocol using injected noise and show that the extracted loss scales as expected with the applied noise strength. The protocol opens access to a higher-frequency spectral window than standard qubit-based spectroscopy and may enable noise characterization during strong driving.

candidates.abstract: We study the conditions under which matrix product states (MPSs) or matrix product operators are exact eigenvectors of an extensive local operator such as a Hamiltonian. By suitably choosing the local operator, this covers a wide range of settings: exact eigenstates of Hamiltonians, including scar states; exact MPS trajectories for driven quantum systems; steady states of local Lindbladians; generalized symmetries of either Hamiltonians or density matrices; and many more. Our key result is that a local, fixed-size equation—namely, how a single term in the operator acts on a block of tensors—provides a necessary and sufficient condition for exact solutions. This local characterization allows us to obtain the full space of MPS solutions to all of the aforementioned problems; in particular, we exemplify the power of our results by recovering the quantum group symmetries of the XXZ model. We also discuss applications to numerical algorithms with MPSs and the generalization of our results to 2D, i.e., projected entangled pair states.

candidates.authors: Wanghao Tian, Bowen Shen, Lizhong Li, Mingjie Zhang, Feng Liu, Chushan Li, Yaotian Liu, Fan Xu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Peiling Li, Li Lu, Yang Xu, Shengwei Jiang, Tingxin Li, Jie Shan, Kin Fai Mak
candidates.abstract: Moiré semiconductors built on angle-aligned transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterobilayers provide a physical realization of the Kondo lattice model, in which one TMD layer is prepared in a Mott insulating state supporting a lattice of local magnetic moments and the other layer in a metallic state supporting itinerant carriers. The symmetry-broken Chern insulator, which exhibits integer quantized Hall conductance at a fractional moiré filling, breaks the translational symmetry of the lattice spontaneously; it also appears only near a magnetic-field-induced Kondo breakdown in the mixed-valence regime of the material. We further demonstrate that the magnetic field required to induce the Kondo breakdown and to stabilize the symmetry-broken Chern insulator is twist angle dependent. The results present new opportunities for exploring the subtle interplay between topology and Kondo interactions in moiré semiconductors.

candidates.abstract: Gravitational waves admit a Stokes decomposition into intensity ($I$), circular polarization ($V$), and linear polarization ($Q$, $U$), analogous to Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarimetry. We show that an intensity-only model is biased when polarized sky components are present, since the detector-network Fisher inner product does not generally make the Stokes responses orthogonal. For transient CBC foregrounds, polarized shot noise is not parametrically suppressed relative to ordinary CBC intensity shot noise. The full Stokes framework separates the Stokes sectors while providing access to polarized anisotropies invisible to conventional intensity-only searches.

candidates.authors: B. De Lucca, P. Ricci, B. Labit, D. Mancini, L. N. Stenger, Z. Tecchiolli
candidates.abstract: Flux-driven two-fluid simulations in a diverted tokamak exhibit a confinement transition when a critical heating threshold is exceeded, as in experimental observations of the L-H transition. The simulations show that electromagnetic drift-wave turbulence spontaneously generates a sheared $E\times B$ flow responsible for transport suppression in the edge. The toroidal-field asymmetry of the transition, here reproduced in simulations for the first time, arises from time-reversal symmetry breaking by finite collisionality, as demonstrated by a quasilinear calculation of the turbulent momentum flux. candidates.title: Realization of Repulsive Polarons in the Strongly Correlated Regime
candidates.authors: R. Henke, J. Levinsen, M. M. Parish, J. Boronat, G. E. Astrakharchik, H. Moritz, C. R. Cabrera
candidates.abstract: Mobile impurities interacting with a quantum medium form quasiparticles known as polarons, a central concept in many-body physics. While the quantum impurity problem has been extensively studied with ultracold atomic gases, repulsive polarons in the strongly correlated regime have remained elusive. Typically, the impurity atoms bind into molecules or rapidly decay into deeper-lying states before they can acquire an appreciable dressing cloud. Here, we report on the realization of polarons in a strongly repulsive two-dimensional quantum gas. Using a superfluid of Li 6 dimers, we introduce impurities by promoting a small fraction of the dimers into higher levels of the transverse confining potential. These novel synthetic-spin polarons give access to the strongly repulsive regime where common decay channels are suppressed. We extract key polaron properties—the energy, quasiparticle residue, and effective mass—using trap modulation and Bragg spectroscopy. Our measurements are well captured by a microscopic T -matrix approach and quantum Monte Carlo simulations, revealing deviations from mean-field predictions. In particular, we measure a significant enhancement of the polaron mass, with values exceeding twice the free-dimer mass. Our demonstration of a stable repulsive Bose polaron establishes a platform for studying impurity physics in low-dimensional and strongly correlated systems.

candidates.title: Temporal Complexity Hierarchies in Solvable Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
candidates.authors: He-Ran Wang, Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Dmitry A. Abanin
candidates.abstract: The influence matrix (IM) provides a powerful framework for characterizing nonequilibrium quantum many-body dynamics by encoding multitime correlations into tensor-network states. Understanding how its computational complexity relates to underlying dynamics is crucial for both theoretical insight and practical utility yet remains largely unexplored despite a few case studies. Here, we address this question for a family of brickwork quantum circuits ranging from integrable to chaotic regimes. Using tools from geometric group theory, we identify three qualitatively distinct scalings of temporal entanglement entropy, establishing a hierarchy of computational resources required for accurate tensor-network representations of the IM for these models. We further analyze the memory structure of the IM and distinguish between classical and quantum temporal correlations. In particular, for certain examples, we identify effectively classical IMs that admit an efficient Monte Carlo algorithm for computing multitime correlations. In more generic settings without an explicit classical description of the IM, we introduce an operational measure of quantum memory with an experimental protocol and discuss examples exhibiting long-time genuinely quantum correlations. Our results establish a new connection between quantum many-body dynamics and group theory, providing fresh insights into the complexity of the IM and its intricate connection to the physical characteristics of the dynamics.
